abstract: The clinical details of two patients with benign mediastinal teratomata are presented. Both patients developed inflammation of the root of the neck, the first after a small dose of radiotherapy and the second after a larger dose of radiotherapy and exploration of the thoracic inlet. In both cases, exploration of the inflamed area was followed by persistent discharge of fluid which was sterile on culture. In the first case, this was found to have a high cholesterol, lipid, and amylase content. In both cases, a benign mixed teratoma, with contents including intestinal epithelium and pancreatic tissue, was removed at thoracotomy. The suggestion is made that leakage of digestive enzymes from pancreatic, intestinal or salivary tissue may be a cause of inflammation in and around teratomata, especially after surgical exploration. Early thoracotomy is advised when the condition is recognized.
abstract_ja: 2例の良性縦隔奇形腫患者の臨床経過を報告する。両者とも放射線療法後、また胸郭入口部の探索後に、頸部根部の炎症を発症した。前者の症例では、炎症部位の探索後に持続的な排液がみられ、無菌培養であった。この液はコレステロール、脂質およびアミラーゼを多く含んでいた。両症例では、腸上皮と膵組織を含む良性混合奇形腫が開胸術で切除された。膵、腸、または唾液腺組織からの消化酵素の漏出が奇形腫の周囲の炎症の原因となる可能性が示唆される。特に外科的探索後に起こりうる。疾患が認識された場合は早期の開胸術が推奨される。
